A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GameNGen and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Retained material can be matched reliably despite renumbering, relocation, and added experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original DOOM simulation results, including PSNR, LPIPS, FVD, human evaluations, and ablations of context length, noise augmentation, training-data policy, and sampling steps.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds long-rollout human evaluations, dataset-size experiments, edited-state generation examples, and a Chrome Dino simulation.

M1.justification: The core diffusion architecture, loss, noise augmentation, decoder fine-tuning, and DOOM inference procedure remain unchanged. Appendix A.10 introduces a bounded adaptation: DQN-based data collection for Chrome Dino and concatenated-episode training sequences that support termination and automatic restart.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates DOOM alone. v2 adds the distinct platform game Chrome Dino, including session termination and restart, and tests DOOM generation from manually edited character placements and level structures absent from training configurations (Appendices A.4 and A.10). This materially extends task and input-condition coverage.

E2.justification: v2 removes the Section 3.3.1 comparison of single-sample generation against four-sample averaging and nearest-median selection. The retained World Models/GameGAN visual comparison and agent-versus-random-policy comparison use the same methods. Newly discussed related works are not added experimental baselines.

E3.justification: Reported agent training changes from 10M to 50M environment steps. v1 describes using all recorded trajectories and generating 900M frames; v2 specifies a random 70M-example subset. These are substantive reported-setting revisions, without establishing reruns. New protocols include 150 three-second comparisons after 5–10 minutes, dataset-size controls, edited-state initialization, and Chrome Dino training with 32-frame context, 256x512 resolution, and 3,000 steps.

E4.justification: v2 adds dataset-size sensitivity experiments using 1M, 5M, 10M, and 70M examples, edited-state generalization case studies, and human evaluation targeting accumulated errors after extended gameplay. Existing context, noise, policy, and sampling-step analyses remain. The brief four-sample averaging/median experiment is removed.

E5.justification: The matched tables retain identical plus/minus reporting. v2 adds no seed counts, repeated-training-run information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or new uncertainty-estimation procedures. Additional human comparisons change evaluation sample size rather than uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 newly reports 50% real-game identification for clips sampled after 5–10 minutes, dataset-size PSNR curves and gameplay findings, edited-scene outcomes, and playable Chrome Dino with automatic restart. These are additional results under new conditions. Existing DOOM headline scores and all three matched tables remain numerically unchanged; the averaging/median qualitative findings disappear.

T1.justification: Section 2 retains the interactive-environment and simulation objectives, and Equation 1 retains the same diffusion loss. Wording and variable-order edits do not alter the mathematics. Neither version provides theoretical results or proofs that are subsequently added, removed, or revised.

C1.justification: The central claim of high-quality, real-time neural game simulation remains. v2 explicitly extends the abstract's human-indistinguishability claim to clips after five minutes of autoregressive generation and emphasizes multi-minute stability. The introduction more explicitly identifies the existing architecture, noise augmentation, decoder tuning, and data collection as contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive qualifications: knowledgeable authors can distinguish the simulation quickly, learned correlations can cause shooting to spawn enemies, and GameNGen cannot easily create entirely new games. It also explains that noise augmentation suppresses small scene edits. These refine the retained discussion of limited memory, exploration coverage, and heuristic state persistence.

D1.justification: New appendices document edited-frame history initialization and Chrome Dino's score-based reward, experience replay, epsilon decay of 0.9995, 2,000 recorded episodes, and episode concatenation. Section 4 revises training-budget and data-use information. Most existing implementation details remain, and the new reproducibility statement does not announce a code or dataset release.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds substantive discussion of VideoGPT, GAIA-1, Diffusion Forcing, and Rolling Diffusion, and updates the existing Alonso discussion with Counter-Strike simulation. It removes stronger contrasts with earlier simulators, while Figure 2 now acknowledges different training data. General graphics and video-diffusion background is retained in Appendix A.9.

P1.justification: v2 revises the abstract, contribution framing, and limitations prose; adds a Broader Impact section; rewrites author contributions; and moves general related-work material into Appendix A.9. These are focused editorial and structural revisions within a largely retained main-section sequence and method/results narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds the dataset-size plot, two edited-state image grids, and the Chrome Dino strip as Figures 13–15 and 18. The sampling-step table moves from v1's appendix to v2's main text, Figures 5–6 are regrouped, and captions and headers change. Existing graphical content and table structures are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: The new human evaluation after extended rollouts addresses an important gap between v1's long-horizon claims and its short-horizon measured comparisons. Chrome Dino, dataset-size experiments, and edited-state studies substantially broaden validation, while clearer failure cases improve interpretation. The new application evidence remains largely qualitative and the training-count revisions are unexplained, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial improvement in empirical support.
